gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sulphur-point: Joystix is all wide-tracked arcade lettering, its stems barely heavier than the arms joining them, and Sulphur Point sits under it. That body keeps one marker-like line weight with bulky, open letters.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-tiktok-sans: Bold and a bit cheeky, Joystix stamps out arcade letters. TikTok Sans follows in a plain sans with a tall x-height and open c, so it can be set a touch smaller without losing its footing.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-ubuntu-sans: Pixel-bright and loud, with room to spare. Joystix is best at grabbing a glance with its mild-contrast arcade capitals, while Ubuntu Sans, with its big lowercase eyes and pipe-like strokes, is best at carrying the actual sentences.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans reads like a ruler-drawn line, with an x-height that fills the space and wide, unclosed terminals on every curve. And Joystix gives it a foil, its arcade letters carrying a faint gradient of weight where the sans-serif has none.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-yaldevi: Chunky arcade swagger up top, with Joystix curves that lighten mildly toward their ends and a compact gap above the x-height. Yaldevi, a sans-serif with outsized lowercase and an e that opens right, reads easily below.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-aldrich: Junegull brings a retro, friendly look with no thick-thin flicker and pinched, closed curves. Aldrich below is a plain sans with a tall x-height and open, cupped rounds, so the two make a clear closed-versus-open contrast.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-alexandria: Lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, that is Junegull's calling card. Alexandria answers it with wide open terminals on a tall, sans body, which makes the pair's strongest quality its plain, friendly clarity.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-amiko: Junegull draws every line as if with one nib, with pinched, closed curves and a retro warmth. Amiko's outward-pointing terminals and chunky lowercase sit open beneath it, so the headline closes in while the text stays loose.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-anek-bangla: Junegull has a signage-like plainness in every line weight, with pinched, closed curves and a retro, friendly feel. Make it small and that heft fades, while Anek Bangla, a sans-serif with wide s curves, would look cramped if blown up large.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-anek-devanagari: Anek Devanagari reads with distinctly open letter mouths and a tall middle zone, a plain sans that lets the eye move easily. Junegull's closed, retro letters give it a friendly counterweight, and their lack of thick-thin contrast is the pair's strongest quality.
